reported_value_text: The primary source reports PPARγ protein in Iba1-positive cells and in sorted lineage-traced myeloid fractions. In the microglial AMPK conditional-knockout experiment, PPARγ was significantly down-regulated in AMPK-flox/flox;Tmem119-CreERT+/- mice receiving L-P, with Figure 6G-J quantified as mean ± SD (n=6) and ** P<0.01 versus the SCI group. In the BV2 inhibitor experiment, blocking AMPK or PGC1α significantly inhibited the PPARγ signal; the Figure 8 western-blot quantification is mean ± SD (n=6), with * P<0.05 and ** P<0.01 versus the L-P group. Exact plotted fluorescence and band-intensity values are not printed in the accessible primary text/captions.

reported_value_text: At 7 days post-SCI, NLRP3 was coexpressed with NeuN, GFAP, AIF1, and OLIG2 markers and increased after SCI. In the time-course Figure 3B comparison versus sham, 7-day NLRP3+/NeuN+ and NLRP3+/GFAP+ cell counts were significantly increased (p=0.0382 and p=0.0028, respectively), and NLRP3+/AIF1+ and NLRP3+/OLIG2+ cells were detected only at 7 days with p=0.0051 and p=0.0029. In the Lcn2 genotype experiment at 7 days, NLRP3/GFAP co-localization was significantly reduced in Lcn2−/− versus WT mice (p=0.0230). Figure 3 reports mean ± SEM and n=3 for immunofluorescence groups; exact image-derived fluorescence/co-localization scalars are not printed. The corresponding Figure 3 western blot reports bulk NLRP3 protein peaking at 7 days versus sham (p=0.0008; n=4 WB), but this queue row is the IF endpoint.

The source reports n=3 injured mice for this staining endpoint.

reported_value_text: Figure 3 reports that at 2 weeks after spinal cord hemisection and 2 weeks of ephrin-A5-Fc treatment, EphA4 immunostaining was markedly reduced in ipsilateral astrocytes adjacent to the injury site compared with control mice; the reduction was not observed further from the injury site or on the contralateral side. The figure reports 100 μm scale bars for panels C-D and 50 μm for E-F; no numeric EphA4 intensity scalar or panel-specific n is printed.

reported_value_text: At day 14 after artery-clamp SCI, Figure 3F reports Smad4 relative protein level normalized to beta-actin across N+con, N+sci, C+con, C+sci, S+con, and S+sci groups. The immunofluorescence analysis used n=4 animals.

Exact band-intensity values were not printed.

reported_value_text: At 6 weeks (42 days) after moderate thoracic contusion SCI, new GFP-positive MBP-positive myelin sheaths around NF200/SMI312-positive axons were 248 +/- 56 sheaths per mm2 in Myrf-inducible conditional knockout mice versus 4664 +/- 674 sheaths per mm2 in controls. At the lesion epicenter, 1.7 +/- 0.4% of myelinated axons in knockout mice had new myelin versus 28.4 +/- 3.0% in controls. The source reports P<0.001 for the six-week between-genotype comparison; values are mean +/- SEM.

reported_value_text: At 24 h after injury, HO-1 co-localized with lectin-positive blood vessels in the lesion epicenter and at 4, 3, and 2 mm rostral to the epicenter, in both gray and white matter. HO-1 was also induced in long, slender processes oriented parallel to the endothelium and in close proximity to the vessel wall; the source describes these as presumably astrocytic foot processes. Primary-antibody omission controls showed no HO-1 immunostaining.

reported_value_text: Figure 3A-B reports increased CD81 expression in equal-volume total plasma EV samples at 1, 3, and 7 days post-injury. The 1-day naive and SCI samples were combined from two independent animal experiments run on separate gels, each with n=3–6/group; the Figure 3B densitometry comparison used n=5–12/group. Figure 3C reports the CD81-per-plasma-EV ratio, calculated as WB densitometry divided by NTA particle count from the same sample; this ratio was markedly increased at 1 and 3 days, with n=5–6/group. Significance was reported versus naive control by Mann–Whitney U test at p<0.05 or p<0.01. Exact CD81 signal and ratio values were not printed.

reported_value_text: Figure 1 reports the 25 kD IgG band (light chain) at the assigned post-injury timepoint. The 25-kD IgG band was significantly elevated within spinal cords after SCI at 1 dpi. After collapsing sexes, SCI increased the band in both 4- and 14-month-old mice; after collapsing ages, SCI increased it in females and males. 14-month-old mice had more signal than 4-month-old mice after SCI. The reported three-way ANOVA injury effect was F(1,32)=36.68, p<0.0001; age effect F(1,32)=22.50, p<0.0001; sex effect F(1,32)=8.72, p<0.01. Printed pairwise p-values included 14-month female versus sex-matched 4-month female p<0.01, and 14-month female injury p<0.001. The figure caption identifies the bands as mouse IgG and reports n=5 per full age-by-sex-by-injury group; collapsed comparisons use n=10. Exact band-intensity values were not printed.

The reported three-way ANOVA injury effect was F(1,32)=41.33, p<0.0001; age effect F(1,32)=40.52, p<0.0001; sex effect F(1,32)=2.943, p=0.10. Printed pairwise p-values included 14-month female versus sex-matched 4-month female p<0.001, 14-month female injury p<0.0001, and 4-month male injury p=0.05. The figure caption identifies the bands as mouse IgG and reports n=5 per full age-by-sex-by-injury group; collapsed comparisons use n=10. Exact band-intensity values were not printed.

reported_value_text: Figure 1 reports the 50 kD IgG band (heavy chain) at the assigned post-injury timepoint. The 50-kD IgG band was significantly elevated within spinal cords after SCI at 3 dpi. After collapsing sexes, SCI increased the band in both 4- and 14-month-old mice; after collapsing ages, SCI increased it in both females and males. 14-month-old mice had more signal than 4-month-old mice after SCI, and female mice had more than male mice. The reported three-way ANOVA injury effect was F(1,32)=46.41, p<0.0001; age effect F(1,32)=37.56, p<0.0001; sex effect F(1,32)=7.36, p<0.01. Printed pairwise p-values included 14-month female versus age-matched male p<0.05, 14-month female versus sex-matched 4-month female p<0.001, and injury effects p<0.0001 for 14-month females and p<0.05 for 4-month and 14-month males. The figure caption identifies the bands as mouse IgG and reports n=5 per full age-by-sex-by-injury group; collapsed comparisons use n=10. Exact band-intensity values were not printed.

reported_value_text: SHP2 was abundantly expressed at the spinal-cord injury site and increased in Iba-1-positive microglia. Figure 1B–C reports SHP2/Iba-1 immunofluorescence at 14 days after SCI as relative fluorescence intensity, with n=5 slices from three mice per group. Figure 1D–E reports a spinal-cord SHP2 Western-blot time course at 1, 7, and 14 days after SCI; SHP2 increased progressively through day 14 and is shown as SHP2/β-actin folds versus control. The blot labels SHP2 at 68 kDa and β-actin at 43 kDa. Exact plotted values were not printed and were not estimated.

Aβ was significantly increased at 1 and 3 days versus sham or naïve samples (p<0.01); naïve and sham mice euthanized 3 days after surgery did not differ. In a separate 3-day DAPT experiment (30 mg/kg orally twice daily beginning 15 min after injury; n=4/group), DAPT attenuated the SCI-induced Aβ increase by 30% (p<0.01). Exact ELISA group concentrations were not printed.

reported_value_text: PS1 immunofluorescence was quantified at the epicenter and 1 and 2 mm rostral and caudal to the injury at 1, 3, and 7 days. At the epicenter, PS1 increased at 1 and 3 days (p<0.02); at 1 mm rostral and caudal it increased at 1 and 3 days (p<0.001 and p<0.005, respectively); at 2 mm rostral and caudal, a significant increase was observed only at 1 day (p<0.0001 and p<0.04, respectively). Figure 2B quantitation used n=3. At 1 day, PS1 was also observed in some Iba1-positive microglia. Exact intensity values and percentages were not printed.
